title: Concepts in Motion: Temporal Concept Bottleneck Model for Interpretable Video Classification
claim: One model turns a video's frames into local concept scores, a global summary, and temporal dependency maps, all interpretable.
layout: Single wide panel: frame strip on top, funnel to outputs, heatmap at right
description: A wide figure with a row of eight video frames across the top, from a movie clip of an archer shooting a bow. Below the frames is a rounded box labeled 'VLM-based Concept Discovery Pipeline'. Under that, a large inverted lavender triangle labeled 'MoTIF' narrows toward the output 'Video Class: Shoot bow'. Beneath the triangle are lists of concepts with scores. On the left, '1. Global Concepts' lists bow +5.211, shoot +1.680 and bend +1.586. Two '2. Local Concepts' lists sit under cream-highlighted columns for particular frame windows, with entries such as bow, mount and shoot. At the far right is a purple-to-yellow attention heatmap titled '(bow)', with query time on the y-axis and key time on the x-axis, labeled '3. Temporal Dependency'. The eye goes first to the frames and the MoTIF triangle.
caption: MoTIF. The method treats videos as windows and produces local concept explanations, global explanations for entire videos, and temporal dependency maps from the attention heads. The model is MoTIF (ViT-L/14) and sample frames are from HMDB51 [ref], licensed under CC BY 4.0.
abstract: Concept Bottleneck Models (CBMs) enable interpretable image classification by structuring predictions around human-understandable concepts, but extending this paradigm to video remains challenging due to the difficulty of extracting concepts and modeling them over time. In this paper, we introduce MoTIF (Moving Temporal Interpretable Framework), a transformer-based concept architecture that operates on sequences of temporally grounded concept activations, by employing per-concept temporal self-attention to model when individual concepts recur and how their temporal patterns contribute to predictions. Central to the framework is a class-conditioned VLM-based concept discovery module that extracts object- and action-centric textual concepts from training videos, yielding temporally expressive concept sets without manual concept annotation. Across multiple video benchmarks, this combination improves over global concept bottlenecks and remains competitive within the interpretable concept-bottleneck setting, while narrowing the gap to strong black-box video baselines that we report as contextual references. Code available at github.com/patrick-knab/MoTIF.
